title: feat(isolation): pluggable secret providers — Infisical runtime injection (docker substrate)
body:
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-15-infisical-secret-provider-design.md` (read the **Re-integration addendum** and **Test Plan** at the end)
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-15-infisical-secret-provider/`
Run: `docs/superpowers/runs/2026-09-14-feat-secrets-injection.yaml` (adopted, fr-goal@1; parked on the manual phase 6)
Resumes: #333

## Summary

Makes secret resolution in `fr.isolation` pluggable behind a `SecretProvider` seam. `env-file`, the default, keeps today's ambient model unchanged. `infisical` fetches secrets at runtime, on demand, inside the devcontainer: `fr isolation exec --secret KEY -- cmd`. Version **4.12.0 → 4.13.0**: a minor bump for the new flag, provider and scaffold options.

This PR was opened in June against fr 3.3 and sat blocked on the cluster (#333). It was rebased onto main 4.3.0 (98 commits), re-integrated, and put through three review rounds. It has since been rebased twice more to keep up with main: onto 4.5.2 on 2026-09-19 and onto **4.12.0 on 2026-09-21**. Both rebases give a linear history with no merge commit.

## What changed since the June version

- **Rebased onto the 4.x isolation targets.** main split isolation into devcontainer, host-worktree and external targets. The June wiring conflicted with that split, so the rebase took main's side of `local.py` / `isolation_cmd.py`. A new TDD phase (5) then rebuilt the wiring on the devcontainer target, with the carried June wiring tests as its RED.
- **`--secret` is devcontainer-only.** In host-worktree and external modes it refuses with an actionable error and runs nothing (operator decision).
- **Per-exec tokens in a per-workspace, contained, read-only-mounted directory:**
  - Each secret-bearing exec writes its own `O_EXCL` `0600` token file under `~/.cache/fr/run-tokens/<repo>/<profile>/<workspace>/` (`0700`).
  - That directory is bind-mounted **read-only** at `/run/fr-secrets`.
  - The wrapper reads the token, then runs `infisical run … -- env -u INFISICAL_TOKEN -- "$@"`, so the user command never sees it.
  - `post_exec` removes that exec's file, whether the command returned or raised.
- **The host follows the committed mount, and the path is contained.**
  - The token directory is parsed from `devcontainer.json`'s `--mount`, as the env-file provider has done since #272.
  - fr refuses any source that isn't exactly three levels under `~/.cache/fr/run-tokens`, or that contains `..`, a symlink or an unresolved variable.
  - Truncation never follows a symlink or blocks on a FIFO the container could plant (`O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`).
- **Teardown and gc:**
  - Token cleanup runs after the container is verified gone (the #354 guarantees are intact).
  - It still runs when the profile config is unreadable.
  - gc's orphan paths also reap token directories, only once the container is confirmed gone.
- **The env-file ensure follows post-#408 main:** a legacy vk mount raises, and files are hardened to `0600`/`0700`.
- **The scaffold composes with the multi-backend `--backend/--host` options:** base install, then forge CLI, then Infisical CLI.
  - `--secret-provider` is validated.
  - `--infisical-*` flags are rejected with env-file.
  - Re-scaffolding to infisical warns about a leftover plaintext env-file.
- **Docs and artifacts:** skill docs rewritten within the 120-line cap; OpenCode/Hermes mirrors regenerated; the plan's `fr_version` migrated and floored to `>=3.7.0,<5.0.0`.

## Security invariants (tested)

- App-secret values never touch host disk. The only host artifact is a short-TTL token in a per-exec `0600` file, removed after its command.
- No secret material on any argv, host or container. The client secret goes via env at mint, the token via the mounted file, and no `--remote-env` is added.
- On demand: no `--secret` means no mint and no profile read. An undeclared key fails before mint, and the CLI exits 2.
- Every interpolated `fr-profiles.yaml` value is `shlex.quote`d, since that file is PR-reachable. Infisical config is validated before minting.
- Back-compat: a profile with no `secret_provider` behaves exactly as before.

## Review findings & fixes

All findings are recorded in `docs/superpowers/journals/plans/2026-06-15-infisical-secret-provider.md`, each with its proving tests.

**June review (phases 1–4), re-checked after the rebase:**
- C1: shell injection via unquoted `project_id`/`env`/`path`. Fixed and carried over.
- C2: the token lingered until `down`. The Target `try/finally` was lost in the rebase and rebuilt in phase 5.
- I1: token cleanup was skipped when the profile config was unreadable. Lost in the rebase, rebuilt.
- I2: an exec could carry `--remote-env`. Rebuilt.
- I3: the CLI install swallowed stderr. Fixed and carried over.
- M1: a mint error could leak stdout. Fixed and carried over.

**Phase-5 review, round 1** (all fixed except one refutation):
- I1: the token directory was shared by every workspace of a profile.
- I2: the host token directory didn't follow the mount.
- I3: a token leaked when `exec_wrap` raised after minting.
- m1: plain exec read the profile.
- m2: cleanup ran before teardown was verified.
- m3: gc orphan paths skipped token cleanup.
- m4: mint had no timeout or empty-token check.
- m5: the user command inherited `INFISICAL_TOKEN`.
- m6: kubernetes-auth read a never-written file.
- m7: scaffold flags weren't validated.
- m8: a leftover env-file got no warning.
- m9: stale prose.
- m10: a constant lived in the wrong module.
- **Refuted — m8 (second half), pin the Infisical CLI install like glab/tea:** Infisical publishes no checksummed static artifact for its apt bootstrap. Its apt repo signing key is the trust anchor, and a code comment marks this as a known v1 limitation.

**Round 2** (containment verification, all fixed):
- V1: the mount source had no containment.
- V2: the gc orphan glob was unguarded.
- V3: label-orphan tokens were reaped before the container was confirmed gone.
- V4: the kubernetes-auth mount directory wasn't created.
- V5: a partial token write leaked.
- V6: `env --` was missing, so a leading `NAME=VALUE` or `-x` user argument was parsed by `env`.
- V7: `${localEnv:VAR:default}` wasn't parsed.
- V8: no test proved `down` follows a non-canonical mount.

**Round 3** (all fixed):
- W1: a symlink or FIFO planted by the container could be followed on truncate. Fixed with the read-only mount plus `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`.
- W2: `..` was collapsed instead of rejected.
- W3: set-but-empty variables should take the default.
- W4: one bad match aborted the gc token reap.
- W5: a vacuous test assertion.

## Decisions

**Operator Q&A (2026-09-14):**
- `--secret` is devcontainer-mode only.
- The live Infisical smoke stays with the operator.
- Rebase and force-push to this PR.
- Hard-tier phases ran on Fable 5.1.

**Process:**
- The Target wiring was rebuilt as a new TDD phase instead of hand-splicing the conflicts.
- Phase 1 carries no walking-skeleton marker: it shipped in June, before the convention existed.

**Known limitations** (in the spec addendum):
- Custom `--path` workspaces that share a basename share a token directory.
- The gc fallback misses orphan token directories of a clone renamed after scaffolding.

**Accepted residual:** a check-then-`rmtree` TOCTOU at teardown, after the container is verified gone.

**Unconfirmed:** the devcontainer CLI's handling of `${localEnv:VAR:default}` for a set-but-empty variable. fr uses `||` semantics. The CLI source wasn't available to check, and the phase-6 smoke pins it. A mismatch fails loudly at `devcontainer up`.

## ⏳ Phase 6: manual and **unimplemented; the operator pushes to this PR**

1. In Infisical (the frank `infisical` namespace), create a **Universal-Auth** machine identity that is **read-only** to the project/path, and set a **short Access-Token TTL** on the identity.
2. On the host, export `FR_INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID` / `FR_INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET` and install the `infisical` CLI. Universal-auth mints host-side.
3. Scaffold an infisical profile, run `fr isolation up` in devcontainer mode, then run the Test Plan item 6 checks below.
4. Record the result with `fr plan edit docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-15-infisical-secret-provider --complete-phase 6 --note "…"`, flip `secret-provider-live-infisical-smoke` to `skipped`, then `fr run resolve 2026-09-14-feat-secrets-injection --step implement-phase --item phase/6 --state done`.

## Test Plan (post-merge, operator-driven)

Every item runs without a live Infisical except item 6. Item numbers match the acceptance-matrix rows listed in brackets.

1. **Back-compat default** [`secret-provider-envfile-default`]. A profile with no `secret_provider` resolves to `EnvFileProvider`. `up_prepare` creates the mounted env-file at `0600` and refuses a legacy vk mount. `exec_wrap` returns an empty wrap.
2. **Scaffold** [`secret-provider-scaffold-infisical`]. `fr init scaffold --secret-provider infisical` writes the `infisical:` block with the default auth env-var names, omits `--env-file`, mounts the token directory, appends the CLI install after any forge-CLI install, and prints the TTL reminder. An env-file profile is unchanged.
3. **On-demand injection** [`secret-provider-infisical-on-demand`]. On the devcontainer target, `exec --secret KEY` puts `infisical run --projectId … --env … --path … --` ahead of the user command and keeps the command intact at the tail. Without `--secret`, nothing is minted and nothing is wrapped. An undeclared key raises before any mint, and the CLI exits 2 having run nothing.
4. **Nothing secret on argv; tokens are per-exec** [`secret-provider-no-secret-on-argv`]. The minted token and the UA client secret appear in no assembled argv (host mint or `devcontainer exec`), and no `--remote-env` is added. Two wraps produce two distinct `0600` token files. `post_exec` removes the file for its own exec, whether the command returned or raised. `down` runs `cleanup`.
5. **Mode scope** [`secret-provider-mode-scope`]. `HostWorktreeTarget.exec` and `ExternalTarget.exec` with non-empty `keys` raise `IsolationError` naming devcontainer mode and run nothing. With empty `keys` they behave as before. The CLI maps the refusal to exit 2.
6. **Live smoke, operator-driven** [`secret-provider-live-infisical-smoke`]. With a real read-only, short-TTL Universal-Auth identity and the two host env vars set: `fr isolation exec --secret KEY -- printenv KEY` prints the value; the same command without `--secret` prints nothing; `INFISICAL_TOKEN` is absent in the child (`exec --secret KEY -- sh -c 'printenv INFISICAL_TOKEN'` prints nothing); and the workspace's token directory is empty afterwards.

## Acceptance

`fr acceptance check`: 112 rows OK (ci 93 / skipped 14 / not-implemented 5).

Rows added since `origin/main`, each with its defense:
- `secret-provider-envfile-default` (**ci**): pins the back-compat promise that every existing profile relies on.
- `secret-provider-scaffold-infisical` (**ci**): the only way an operator creates an infisical profile, so its shape must not drift.
- `secret-provider-infisical-on-demand` (**ci**): the feature's core promise, that secrets are fetched only when asked for.
- `secret-provider-no-secret-on-argv` (**ci**): the security invariant the design depends on, ps-visible argv and per-exec tokens.
- `secret-provider-mode-scope` (**ci**): pins the operator's devcontainer-only decision, so `--secret` can't silently run unwrapped on a pod.
- `secret-provider-live-infisical-smoke` (**not-implemented**): needs a real Infisical identity, so it is operator-owned phase 6 and can't run in CI.

The existing repo-wide debt (14 skipped, 4 other not-implemented rows) is unchanged by this PR.

## Verification

**GitHub CI is the authoritative run.**

**Rebased onto `origin/main` at 4.12.0 on 2026-09-21** (33 commits, linear), after main landed the unit-record run model (#508), isolation reap guards (#507), OpenCode phase-executor and tier dispatch (#495, #504, #506) and the executor-handoff bounds (#514). Beyond the replay:
- **The previous 4.6.0 bump was dropped** and replaced by one bump from main's tip to 4.13.0.
- **Reconciled against main afterwards.** The rebase took this branch's side on generated and append-structured files so it could keep moving, and each one was then rebuilt from main:
  - `matrix.yaml`: main's file plus the six `secret-provider-*` rows (177 rows).
  - `fr-init` and `fr-isolation` SKILL.md: main's versions, including the gh-486 host wording and status line v2, with the Infisical and `--secret` edits re-applied, at exactly 120 lines each. Only these two skills and their mirrors differ from main.
  - The OpenCode and Hermes mirrors and all three acceptance reports were regenerated.
- **Run cursor migrated** through main's new hops, including the 4 → 5 unit-record rewrite. `fr run status` reads it back cleanly.
- **Privacy check:** this branch's spec, plan, journals, run file, matrix rows and PR body contain no third-party identifiers (per the new third-party-privacy rule).

Full local suite at the rebased head: **4052 passed, 85 skipped**. The one earlier failure, the unarchived-plans tripwire, cleared once the branch was rebased on #520. Ruff, format and mypy are clean. Other local checks at the rebased head: `fr validate artifacts` on all 53 artifacts, `fr acceptance check` with 177 rows OK, journal checks clean, plan self-review passes, and `fr harness parity --check` plus the skill tripwires pass.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Explainers:** the fr-goal explainer lists "Profile secrets → `~/.config/fr/secrets/<repo>/<profile>.env`". That stays true, because env-file is the default and Infisical is opt-in, so no explainer change is needed. `fr-isolation.html` has no committed source (a known gap) and doesn't describe secrets.
- **Unarchived-plans tripwire:** main was briefly red on three merged-but-unarchived plans. #520 archived them, and this branch is rebased on top of #520, so the tripwire passes here.

## Ready checklist

- [x] CI green on the 4.13.0 head `da0409c` (all checks pass, merge state CLEAN)
- [x] Taken out of draft by the operator
- [ ] Operator review of the 2026-09-21 rebase (a history rewrite after the earlier OK)
